# Introduction

## Motivation

Statistical inference is the process of drawing conclusions from data. Consider a simple example: estimating the probability of a coin landing heads.

::: {.callout-note}
This chapter provides a first look at the core ideas. Later chapters develop the theory and computation in depth.
:::

## A first example

Suppose we flip a coin $n$ times and observe $k$ heads. The maximum likelihood estimate of the probability $p$ of heads is:

$$
\hat{p} = \frac{k}{n}
$$

We can simulate this in Python:

```{python}
#| label: fig-coin-simulation
#| fig-cap: "MLE estimate of coin bias converges as sample size grows."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
true_p = 0.6
n_flips = 1000

flips = rng.binomial(1, true_p, size=n_flips)
cumulative_estimate = np.cumsum(flips) / np.arange(1, n_flips + 1)

plt.plot(cumulative_estimate, label=r"$\hat{p}$")
plt.axhline(true_p, color="red", linestyle="--", label=f"True $p = {true_p}$")
plt.xlabel("Number of flips")
plt.ylabel("Estimated probability")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Convergence of MLE")
plt.show()
```
